header_summary:
A proposal has been introduced to enhance wallet recovery workflows by embedding BIP39 mnemonics and optional passphrases directly within output script descriptors, streamlining secure and interoperable restoration processes for Bitcoin wallets. This approach, detailed in a [pull request](https://github.com/polespinasa/bips/pull/2) and tested via [Bitcoin Core implementation](https://github.com/polespinasa/bitcoin/pull/8), enables accurate derivation of keys and supports complex key expression scenarios.

Within the Elements project, a Hybrid Key Encapsulation (HKE) mechanism has been proposed, combining secp256k1 ECDH and ML-KEM-768 cryptographic paths using a UG combiner as per the CFRG draft [draft-irtf-cfrg-hybrid-kems-12](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-irtf-cfrg-hybrid-kems-12/). This hybrid design, outlined in the [ELIP pull request](https://github.com/ElementsProject/ELIPs/pull/46), strengthens post-quantum security while maintaining compatibility with established standards.

Recent analysis of Bitcoin’s unspent transaction outputs (UTXOs) at block 975,019 reveals that 35.6% of all BTC reside in outputs whose keys or scripts have already been exposed on-chain, with detailed breakdowns available in [extraction rules documentation](https://github.com/duncan0k/btc-exposure-index/blob/2a0f4b053cad2ae3dc101a4e4c154ac2b4706f25/docs/extraction-rules.md11-relation-to-the-bip-362-draft). Notable key reuse patterns and exposure distributions by output type were identified, providing crucial insights for ongoing standards development.

The spscand tool, described at the [spscand GitHub repository](https://github.com/ZenulAbidin/spscand), offers privacy-focused scanning for BIP352 silent payments, supporting multiple block data sources, strict proxy isolation, and efficient detection of relevant outputs without risking key exposure. Its underlying C library, libspscan, enables seamless integration into other wallets, ensuring robust privacy and correctness through comprehensive testing.

Advancements in UTXO snapshot hash computation leverage Merkle trees and periodic cryptographic proofs, as outlined in [BIP452](https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0452.mediawiki), to optimize blockchain validation and facilitate privacy-preserving proof of reserves using zero-knowledge techniques.

Additionally, the mining simulation project has incorporated 2026 values, bug fixes, and improved stale rate analysis in its [repository](https://github.com/darosior/miningsimulation), with ongoing work to model internal delays for evaluating Stratum V2 efficiency, as discussed in the [issue thread](https://github.com/darosior/miningsimulation/issues/2).

recent_posts.title: [BIP Draft] bip39() Descriptor Key Expression
recent_posts.summary: - The proposal introduces key expressions in output script descriptors for mnemonic-based wallet recovery.  - Direct inclusion of mnemonics and passphrases in descriptors facilitates standardized and secure wallet restoration.  - Draft details and implementation are available online for testing, with feedback actively requested.

recent_posts.title: BIP Proposal: ML-KEM Key Establishment
recent_posts.summary: - Hybrid Key Encapsulation employs a UG combiner to integrate secp256k1 ECDH and ML-KEM-768 methods.  - The construction achieves IND-CCA security if at least one cryptographic path remains secure.  - This hybrid approach improves post-quantum readiness while preserving compatibility with existing cryptographic standards.

recent_posts.title: spscand and libspscan: a watch-only BIP352 scanner
recent_posts.summary: - spscand enables detection of BIP352 silent payments while minimizing information leakage and preserving user privacy.  - Supports three block sources and uses SOCKS5 proxy isolation, batch processing, and SipHash-protected lookups.  - Performance, correctness, and privacy are validated through mainnet tests, BIP352 test vectors, and real-world scenarios.

recent_posts.title: How much BTC sits behind keys or scripts already on chain (block 975,019)
recent_posts.summary: - About 35.6% of all Bitcoin UTXOs are exposed, mainly via specific output types and rules.  - Key reuse across output forms is substantial, with notable overlaps and many reused public keys.  - Some outputs remain unmeasured due to specification ambiguities, but sampling shows minimal overlooked exposure.

recent_posts.title: A STARK proof of Bitcoin's UTXO set at block 972,500, with circuits proven in Lean
recent_posts.summary: - Efficient UTXO snapshot hash computation enables scalable, verifiable blockchain validation with Merkle trees and MMR.  - Data restructuring and standardized hashing facilitate faster, cheaper proof generation and parallel block validation.  - Per-UTXO Merkle trees support independent proof verification and privacy-preserving reserves proof using zkproofs.

recent_posts.title: Propagation Delay and Mining Centralization: Modeling Stale Rates
recent_posts.summary: - The mining simulation project now includes 2026 values and bug fixes from Fable.  - Expanded README documentation analyzes the impact of stale rates on mining profitability.  - Future model extensions may address internal delays and evaluate Stratum V2 efficiency benefits.

today_in_history_posts.title: OP_CHECKWILDCARDSIGVERIFY or "Wildcard Inputs" or "Coalescing Transactions"
today_in_history_posts.summary: - Small UTXOs from multiple donations increase transaction fees due to numerous listed inputs.  - The proposed OP_CHECKWILDCARDSIGVERIFY opcode enables combining these UTXOs into a single output.  - Using a wildcard input with this method significantly reduces transaction fees.

today_in_history_posts.title: Payment channel without timeout protected from malleability
today_in_history_posts.summary: - A requests B’s pubkey and creates the initial commitment transaction to begin the process.  - A has B sign a hash required for broadcasting, without revealing the commitment details to B.  - B cannot identify A’s anchor before announcement due to lack of P2SH multisig information.

today_in_history_posts.title: Can block validation benefit from CUDA?
today_in_history_posts.summary: - Validating each transaction within a block is resource-intensive and currently uses all CPU threads.  - Employing CUDA computing and GPUs could significantly improve transaction validation speed and efficiency.  - Utilizing parallel computing may enhance node performance and contribute to blockchain system robustness.
